analysis.investment_thesis: GPPL is a high-quality, near-monopoly port asset with a 23% ROIC and near-zero leverage, but the Magic Formula demands BOTH quality AND cheapness — at a ~7.4% earnings yield (EBIT ₹578 Cr / EV ~₹7,833 Cr), the stock simply isn't priced at a bargain. Revenue growth at just 4.6% CAGR over 9 years with zero volume expansion in FY25 limits the upside case.
key_strengths: High ROIC ~23% (EBIT ₹578 Cr / Capital Employed ~₹2,461 Cr) — a genuinely good business above the 20% threshold
Near-monopoly port infrastructure in Gujarat with AP Moller-Maersk as promoter, near-zero debt (D/E: 0.02), and 43.8% operating margins
Consistent FCF generation (₹312–417 Cr/yr over last 3 years) with 5/5 positive OCF years
key_risks: Revenue was completely flat FY24 vs FY25 (both ₹988 Cr) — stagnation at the top line undermines any growth premium in valuation
Earnings yield of ~7.4% is well below the Magic Formula's 12% attractiveness threshold — the stock is fairly valued, not cheap
FY25 net profit boosted by ₹98 Cr 'Other Income' vs typical ₹30–35 Cr — normalized earnings yield is likely even lower (~6.5%)
red_flags: Revenue flat in FY25 despite a decade of minimal growth (4.6% CAGR) — the business is maturing with limited volume expansion
Other Income spike in FY25 (₹98 Cr vs ₹31 Cr prior year) inflates reported profit — normalized EPS is meaningfully lower
Earnings yield at ~7.4% fails the Magic Formula's minimum screen; the market is already pricing in the quality
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Running the Magic Formula: EBIT is ₹578 Cr (operating income FY25), Enterprise Value = Market Cap ₹7,782.5 Cr + Debt ₹63 Cr – Cash ₹13 Cr = ~₹7,833 Cr, giving an Earnings Yield of 7.4%. That's barely above the 6% "avoid" floor and well below the 12%+ that the formula requires for a buy. ROIC (proxied by the given ROCE of 23.3%) clears the 20% threshold, confirming this is genuinely a good business. But with only one of two formula legs passing, the stock earns a mediocre ranking — "good business, wrong price."

On the business itself, GPPL has real moat characteristics: infrastructure monopoly, a strategic global promoter (Maersk), pristine balance sheet, and 44% operating margins. The FCF conversion is excellent at ~60–80% of net profit. However, the stagnation concern is real — revenue of ₹988 Cr in both FY24 and FY25 after a decade of sub-5% CAGR suggests the port is running near capacity without major capacity expansion. The FY25 PAT of ₹397 Cr includes a suspicious ₹98 Cr other income (vs. ₹31 Cr in FY24). Stripping that out, normalized PAT would be closer to ₹330–340 Cr, implying a P/E of ~23x — fair for the quality, but not a bargain. Hold and revisit if the stock pulls back to sub-₹130 (earnings yield >10%).
